text:
I need to send a quarterly update to our investors. I'm the founder of a scheduling app for physical therapy clinics. We have 6 people.

Numbers for the quarter:
- Monthly recurring revenue is $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- We added 9 clinics and lost 4. One of the 4 was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain that paid $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system.
- We have $480,000 in the bank and lose about $44,000 a month.
- Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started.
- I didn't send updates for the last two quarters.
- Next month we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month.

Under 500 words. It goes to 11 investors.

Before I draft this, here's how I'd build the argument and the gaps I'd like you to fill.

**The argument as it stands**

- **Claim:** The core business held steady through a hard quarter, and the standalone reminder product is the next step. You'll report on it against a clear checkpoint.
- **Grounds:** MRR stayed at $41,000 even though you lost your largest customer ($5,500/month, about 13% of revenue). That means new business replaced it. You added 9 clinics and lost 4. Clinics using reminders went from 13% no-shows to 7%, nearly halving them.
- **Link:** If clinics will pay for a measurable cut in no-shows, the reminder feature can sell on its own, including to clinics locked into their records system's scheduler.
- **What investors will raise:**
  1. Runway is about 11 months ($480k ÷ $44k).
  2. Flat MRR means no growth.
  3. Records systems are bundling scheduling, so how many more chains will leave?
  4. You went silent for two quarters.
- **Scale of the bet:** Covering the $44k monthly burn with reminders alone would take about 290 customers at $150.

**Questions (most important first)**

1. **What's the plan for the runway?** With about 11 months left, investors will read everything else through this. Are you raising, cutting burn, or aiming for break-even? Is there an ask for these 11 people, like intros, a bridge, or advice?
2. **What can you commit to for the reminder product?** For example, a number of paying customers by a date, and what you'll do if you miss it. I won't make one up, so it has to come from you.
3. **What evidence is there that clinics will buy reminders on their own?** A waitlist, pilot clinics, conversations, or clinics that left (like the chain) saying they'd pay for reminders alone? This is the best answer to the bundling threat.
4. **How solid is the no-show figure?** How many clinics and over how long? Investors will ask whether it's 3 clinics or 30.
5. **Why no updates for two quarters, and should the email say so?** I'd suggest one plain sentence near the top, acknowledging the gap and committing to quarterly updates. Tell me if you'd rather say it differently.
6. **Is there anything else they'll find out anyway?** For example, what MRR did over the two missed quarters, whether other customers use the records-system scheduler, or any team changes.

If you don't know an answer, just say so and I'll write the update without that point rather than guess.

1. I don't know yet on raising vs cutting vs break-even. The ask for investors is 20 minutes on the phone with each of them, and intros to clinic chains.

2. I can't commit to a customer number by a date. What I can commit to: an update the first week of every quarter from now on (next one January 7), and a monthly one-page set of numbers for any investor who asks.

3. 6 clinics have said they'll buy the reminder feature on its own when it launches December 1.

4. I don't know the clinic count or time period off hand.

5. I skipped them because the numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. No other reason. One plain sentence near the top is fine.

6. Two of our other customers use the same records system as the chain that left. Together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way. I don't know the MRR for the two missed quarters, and there are no team changes.

I've written the update below. It's about 400 words.

- **Recent sales:** I didn't add up the past quarter's new sales. With MRR flat, that would mean subtracting the $5,500 loss and also guessing at the other three customers you lost, so I just say revenue held steady.
- **No-show figure:** I left out the sample size because you don't have it to hand. The 13% to 7% drop is your strongest number, so expect investors to ask how many clinics it covers and over what period. If you can get those two figures, add them in one short sentence after it.
- **The six launch clinics:** together they're $900 a month. I said plainly that this is a start and doesn't close the gap. Investors will do that maths anyway, so it's better they see you've done it.
- **Signature and subject:** I didn't put a quarter label in the subject or a name under the sign-off. Add both before sending.

Subject: Investor update — November 2026

Hi all,

This is our first update in six months. I skipped the last two because the numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. That was the wrong call. From now on you'll get an update in the first week of every quarter, and the next one is January 7.

In short, revenue held steady even though we lost our largest customer. We have about 11 months of runway. On December 1 we start selling our text reminders as a standalone product. I'd like 20 minutes on the phone with each of you before the end of the year.

**Numbers**
- MRR: $41,000, the same as three months ago
- Customers: 9 added, 4 lost
- Cash: $480,000
- Net burn: about $44,000 a month, which gives us roughly 11 months

**The customer we lost**
Our largest customer was a 12-clinic chain paying $5,500 a month, about 13% of revenue. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system. New clinics made up the loss, which is why MRR is flat and not down.

That risk hasn't gone away. Two other customers use the same records system, and together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way. Records systems that come with their own scheduler are the biggest threat to our core product.

**What we're doing about it**
Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, down from 13% before they started. That cuts missed appointments almost in half, and it's the result clinics care about most.

From December 1 we'll sell reminders on their own for $150 a month. A clinic won't need to use our scheduler to get them, so we can keep selling to clinics whose records system already includes one. Six clinics have told us they'll buy at launch. That's $900 a month. It's a start, but it doesn't close the gap to our burn. I'm not putting a customer target on it yet. You'll see actual numbers on January 7.

**Runway**
I haven't decided yet whether we raise, cut burn or aim for break-even. If nothing changes, we run out of cash in about 11 months, so I need to decide soon. I'd value your views before I do.

**Two asks**
1. **20 minutes on the phone.** Please reply with a time that works for you. I'd like to talk through the runway decision with each of you.
2. **Introductions to physical therapy clinic chains.** They're the buyers for both the scheduler and the standalone reminders.

If you'd like a one-page set of numbers every month, reply and I'll add you to the list.

Thank you for your patience over the last six months.
